title: Channels, SQS, and in-process message passing
hook: When your API receives a webhook or order, you often want to process it asynchronously without blocking the HTTP response. In-process System.Threading.Channels decouple producers from consumers inside one app; Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) does the same across services and survives restarts.

blocks.text: System.Threading.Channels provides bounded or unbounded async queues: producers call WriteAsync, consumers use await foreach or ReadAsync. Multiple reader tasks compete safely for items. Amazon SQS is a managed message queue: producers SendMessage, consumers ReceiveMessage with visibility timeout, and DeleteMessage after successful processing. In ASP.NET Core, a common pattern is an HTTP endpoint that enqueues work (channel or SQS) and a BackgroundService that dequeues and processes with IServiceScopeFactory per message.

entries.plainDefinition: In-process async producer-consumer queue with optional bounded capacity for backpressure.
Managed cloud queue with at-least-once delivery, visibility timeout, and dead-letter queues.
entries.example: await sqs.SendMessageAsync(new SendMessageRequest { QueueUrl = url, MessageBody = json });

entries.plainDefinition: Period after ReceiveMessage when the message is hidden from other consumers; extend or delete on success.
entries.example: Default 30s — must exceed max processing time or message reappears

entries.plainDefinition: Queue for messages that failed processing after max receive count — prevents infinite retry loops.

blocks.text: Returning 202 Accepted and processing in the background improves API latency and absorbs traffic spikes. Channels are zero-infrastructure for single-instance dev and low-volume prod. SQS adds durability, horizontal scaling across pods, and decoupling when the API and worker deploy separately. Choosing wrong tool — unbounded channel in production with no memory cap — causes out-of-memory crashes under load.

blocks.title: At-least-once delivery
blocks.body: SQS delivers messages at least once. Your handler must be idempotent — use deduplication keys, database unique constraints, or conditional updates. Never assume exactly-once without the outbox pattern or idempotent consumer design.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: HTTP endpoint enqueues
items.body: POST /orders returns 202; serializes event to SQS SendMessage.

items.title: BackgroundService polls
items.body: ReceiveMessage with long polling (WaitTimeSeconds=20) reduces empty responses.

items.title: Process with scoped DI
items.body: CreateScope per message; resolve DbContext and handlers; process idempotently.

items.title: Delete or extend
items.body: DeleteMessage on success. On failure, let visibility timeout expire for retry or move to DLQ.

diagram.title: Channel vs SQS architecture

flowchart LR

snippet.label: Bounded channel with BackgroundService consumer
snippet.explanation: Bounded channel with Wait mode applies backpressure — producers slow down when consumers lag. Singleton channel registered in DI. Consumer creates scope per message.

snippet.label: SQS producer from minimal API
snippet.explanation: Return 202 Accepted immediately. SQS carries the work. FIFO queues need MessageGroupId and MessageDeduplicationId for ordering and dedup.

snippet.label: SQS consumer with idempotent processing
snippet.explanation: Long polling reduces cost and latency. Visibility timeout must exceed processing time. Delete only on success. Failed messages retry automatically.

snippet.label: Diagnostics — channel depth and SQS metrics
snippet.explanation: Monitor queue depth in production. Channel.Reader.Count for in-process backpressure. SQS CloudWatch metrics for cross-service queues. Age of oldest message is the key SLO indicator.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Unbounded channel in production — memory grows unbounded under spike. Deleting SQS message before processing completes. Visibility timeout shorter than max processing time — duplicate processing. No idempotency on at-least-once delivery. Sharing one DbContext scope across parallel SQS message handlers.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: CloudWatch ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage and DLQ depth alarms. OpenTelemetry trace from HTTP enqueue span to consumer ProcessMessage span with same correlation id in message attributes. dotnet-counters threadpool-queue-length if channel consumer is CPU-bound. Load test: spike POST /orders, verify p95 HTTP stays low while queue depth grows then drains. Poison message: after maxReceiveCount lands in DLQ — alert and manual replay tool.

blocks.title: Channel vs SQS vs outbox
rows: Single instance, dev, low volume co-hosted
Must not lose message if API crashes after commit

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Claiming SQS is exactly-once without idempotent handlers. Unbounded in-memory queue for production traffic. Not knowing visibility timeout causes duplicate delivery. Unable to explain when outbox beats direct SQS send after database commit.

interviewTakeaways: Channel<T> decouples producers and consumers in-process; SQS provides durable at-least-once delivery across services.
SQS requires idempotent consumers — visibility timeout and retries cause duplicates; use DLQ for poison messages.
Production tip: bounded channels with backpressure; SQS long polling; alert on ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage.

60s: Endpoint returns 202, enqueues to channel or SQS. BackgroundService polls with scoped DI per message. Delete SQS message only on success. Bounded channel for backpressure. Outbox when DB and message must be atomic.
Follow-up: how does the outbox pattern solve the dual-write problem between database and SQS?
commonPitfalls: Saying SQS is exactly-once gets you rejected — it is at-least-once; idempotency is mandatory.
Unbounded Channel in production — memory exhaustion under traffic spike.

Strong answer: 'Bounded channel for co-hosted dev/small prod. SQS for multi-pod with long poll, visibility timeout > processing time, DLQ after 5 retries. IServiceScopeFactory per message. Outbox when event must survive API crash with DB commit.'
